articles.title: Nvidia's relationship with China just got even more complicated as report says Jensen Huang was target of spy plot
articles.summary: Recent media reports have highlighted Nvidia's delicate relationship with China.
articles.body:
Nvidia's ( NVDA ) business is booming, but one sector of the market remains a seemingly impenetrable morass for the world's leading chip designer: China.

For years, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has struggled to gain a foothold in the world's second-largest economy, due in large part to restrictions imposed by the Department of Commerce, which regulates international chip sales. Seeking inroads, Huang has repeatedly urged the White House to loosen those restrictions, which the administration says are necessary for national security and for the US to remain ahead in the AI race.

When Nvidia last reported earnings, forward guidance once again omitted sales projections for China, continually snarled by state politics.

The complicated relationship between Nvidia and China was thrust back into public light on Thursday after the New York Times reported new US intelligence efforts. The US intelligence service, the report says, believes a Chinese national named Alice Huang — who has served as a leader of Nvidia chip customer Megaspeed and who maintains a well-documented relationship with Huang himself — has acted as an intelligence asset and passed information to the governing party in Beijing.

The reporting raises major questions about potential information leakage from Nvidia to China, not only regarding trade secrets but also about Jensen Huang's increasingly deep ties to the White House as he has lobbied for eased restrictions. At a company event in September, Huang took a call from Trump on stage, putting the US leader on speakerphone as Trump dismissed fears around AI's security implications as a "scam."

The race between the US and China to develop and disseminate their own AI technology has, over the past several years, become a paramount concern for the leadership of both governments.

While China has matched or even surpassed the US on the development and distribution of "open weight" AI models, which often come at far cheaper costs than "closed weight" alternatives, the US frontier labs such as Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) have retained the lead in developing the most advanced models.

Powering those advanced models are chips designed by Nvidia, whose leading semiconductors are often regarded as the gold standard for computing performance. While the chips are hugely popular in the US and other global markets, the Commerce Department has, since 2022, blocked Nvidia from selling successive generations of its chips to Chinese buyers as Washington seeks to maintain its edge over Beijing.

articles.title: ADT stock surges to 5-year high after Thrive Holdings agrees to $7.6 billion buyout deal
articles.summary: Home security company ADT agreed on Thursday to be acquired and taken private by Thrive Holdings in an all-cash deal that values the company at $7.6 billion.
articles.body:
Home security company ADT ( ADT ) agreed on Thursday to be acquired and taken private by Thrive Holdings in an all-cash deal that values the company at $7.6 billion.

Thrive Holdings will pay $10 per share in cash for ADT, representing a 45.6% premium over ADT stock's closing price on Oct. 27.

ADT stock soared 34% to around $9.93 per share on the news, putting it on pace for its highest close since August 2021.

Thrive Holdings is a private capital group founded by Josh Kushner and backed by OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ), focused on acquiring enterprise businesses for the long term and advancing their artificial intelligence and technological capabilities.

Thrive currently operates 75 businesses across accounting, IT services, and the built environment.

"ADT has spent generations showing up for people when it matters most," Thrive Holdings partner Kareem Zaki said in a press release . "We intend to build on that foundation by strengthening ADT's technology and product capabilities, with the capital and patience to invest over decades. Our ambition is to help ADT's teams better serve customers and offer a seamless service with more actionable information for the professionals responding."

This story is developing. Check back for updates.

articles.title: Alphabet heads for a $500 billion drop in market value, the biggest in its history
articles.summary: Alphabet is on track for its worst day ever, with nearly $500 billion in market value at stake, the second-biggest one-day wipeout for a US-listed stock.
articles.body:
Alphabet ( GOOGL ) is on track for its worst day ever. The stock fell about 13% Thursday after its third quarter results , steeper than any session since it went public in 2004, including its drops in March 2020 and September 2008.

At its low, Alphabet had lost $524 billion in stock market value, the second-biggest one-day loss ever for a US-listed company. Only Nvidia ( NVDA ) has lost more, about $593 billion on Jan. 27, 2025, the day China's DeepSeek rattled AI investors.

Alphabet would need to close at about $274.75, down roughly 15%, to take Nvidia's record, by Yahoo Finance calculations. A close at $282.34 or lower would lock in a full $500 billion loss. It has already blown past the $400 billion SpaceX (SPCX) lost on June 22, the previous No. 2.

In dollars, it's Alphabet's worst day by far. Its previous worst was about $275 billion on July 23. It's also on track for the stock's steepest drop after an earnings report since the company went public, according to Bespoke Investment Group . The previous low was a slide of nearly 10% in July 2008.

The quarter gave both sides plenty to argue over. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to about $31 billion, and the Gemini app passed 1 billion users. But search revenue grew 12% to about $63 billion, short of Wall Street's roughly $65 billion estimate. Free cash flow — the cash left after paying for things like data centers — swung to a loss of about $9 billion as AI spending climbed. The company's stakes in AI labs cost it too.

"The bears will argue this is the first quarter that AI is starting to seriously hurt their search business," Pivotal Research CEO Jeffrey Wlodarczak said in a rundown of why investors hated the quarter .

CFRA's Angelo Zino was more patient, telling Yahoo Finance the pullback "probably represents a buying opportunity."

US-listed stocks have shed $200 billion or more in a single session 18 times this year through Wednesday. That's up from 13 in all of 2025 and none before 2022, according to Yahoo Finance calculations from Bloomberg data. Alphabet alone has lost about $1.4 trillion since its record in May.

Amazon ( AMZN ) reports after Thursday's close, the last of the big three cloud providers to report this week. Faster growth at Amazon Web Services without a hit to cash flow would point to a problem specific to Google's search business. Another quarter of cash burn would put the whole AI spending trade back on the defensive.

articles.title: Intel tops Q3 earnings estimates, but falls short of Q4 outlook on sluggish PC sales as stock plunges 20%
articles.summary: Intel reported better than anticipated Q3 earnings after the bell Thursday, but it's Q4 outlook fell short of expectations.
articles.body:
Intel ( INTC ) reported better-than-anticipated third-quarter earnings after the bell Thursday, but Q4 revenue outlook fell short of Wall Street's expectations on declining PC sales.

Intel stock fell more than 20% on the news.

In the fourth quarter, Intel is projecting revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, well below the $17 billion analysts expected.

Intel says the shortfall is a result of a worse-than-anticipated drop in PC revenue. The industry is contending with two overlapping factors at the moment: difficult comparisons to last year, when Microsoft ended support for Windows 10, forcing enterprises around the world to purchase newer Windows 11 systems, and the steady increase in PC prices, which is eating into demand.

At the same time, a deadly explosion at an Intel plant in Israel, unrelated to the war, will limit Intel's ability to meet demand. The incident is expected to account for roughly $300 million of the Q4 revenue miss.

For Q3, Intel saw adjusted earnings (EPS) of $0.52, ahead of EPS projections of $0.41. Revenue was in line with estimates of $16.5 billion and up 21% year over year.

This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

Intel's Intel Product segment, which includes sales of its data center and PC processors, came in at $15.4 billion versus an estimate of $15.5 billion. PC chip sales hit $8.1 billion, missing a target of $8.8 billion. Data center sales, however, helped buoy the segment, topping $7.3 billion in the quarter, up from a projected $6.6 billion.

AI is driving strong demand for Intel's data center central processing units (CPUs). And that demand is continuing to increase as more AI agents come online.

Intel's Foundry business, its chip manufacturing arm, generated $6.7 billion in Q3, ahead of Wall Street's $6.1 billion estimate and up 58% year over year.

Intel's foundry business is reportedly beginning to sign big-name customers, with The Information reporting that Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) placed an order with the company to produce 3 million of its custom Tensor Processing Units. Nvidia is also reportedly in talks with Intel to build its chips.

According to Reuters , Intel is also in discussions with SK Hynix about a deal that could see the memory chip maker lease space at Intel's Ohio manufacturing facility.

articles.title: Rivian reports upbeat Q3 results, boosts full-year guidance as R2 sales ramp up
articles.summary: Rivian reported third quarter results after the bell on Thursday
articles.body:
Rivian ( RIVN ) reported upbeat third quarter results after the bell on Thursday and boosted its guidance, citing strong R2 sales.

Rivian reported Q3 revenue of $2.155 billion vs. $2.02 billion per Bloomberg consensus, up 38% from a year ago. Rivian posted an adjusted loss per share of $0.48 vs. $0.61, and an adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) loss of $435 million vs. $575.9 million, narrower than the $602 million loss from last year.

Rivian also reported a gross profit of $176 million, up $152 million from a quarter ago, though the automotive segment remained negative.

This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

More importantly, Rivian improved its full-year profit guidance, now seeing an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.75 billion to $1.85 billion (prior $1.8 billion to $2 billion) and trimmed capital expenditures to $1.40 billion to $1.50 billion (prior $1.7 billion to $1.8 billion), topping analyst expectations of an EBITDA loss of $1.88 billion and capital expenditures of $1.75 billion, respectively.

Rivian also raised its full-year delivery guidance to 67,000 - 70,000 (prior 65,000 to 70,000 vehicles), topping analysts' consensus estimates of 67,227.

"We had great results with R2 becoming our bestselling vehicle by volume in the third quarter. Customer and media feedback on R2 has been exceptional," CEO RJ Scaringe said in a statement. "Regarding our technology roadmap, our autonomy platform is progressing rapidly, and we are super excited about Point to Point [self-driving]."

Earlier this month, Rivian said it produced 19,751 vehicles at its plant in Normal, Illinois, and delivered 19,248 during the quarter, topping Bloomberg estimates of 18,952 and 18,902, respectively. Deliveries jumped 46% from a year ago and 58% from Q2, with R2 deliveries, which began in June, most likely fueling the growth.

Rivian's cash position is also in the spotlight. Rivian ended the quarter with $5.502 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, with $6.095 billion of total liquidity including a revolving credit facility.

articles.title: Reddit to Limit Access for Logged-Out Users in Strategy Shift
articles.summary: Reddit Inc. said it plans to shift to a primarily logged-in user experience as the social forum seeks to deepen engagement and improve the advertising busine...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Reddit Inc. said it plans to shift to a primarily logged-in user experience as the social forum seeks to deepen engagement and improve the advertising business that continues to drive its solid earnings results.

On Thursday, as the company posted third-quarter sales that beat analyst expectations, Chief Executive Officer Steve Huffman announced that Reddit will eventually limit how much of the platform people can access without an account. The company plans to start testing different approaches in markets outside of the US throughout the fourth quarter, and hasn't decided yet which parts of its site will remain available to logged-out visitors.

The strategy marks a big shift for the company, which has allowed users to explore its forums without an account for two decades. Reddit executives are willing to sacrifice some of the platform's reach to engage a smaller but more engaged audience with insights that will be valuable to advertisers.

In an interview on Thursday, Chief Operating Officer Jen Wong acknowledged the potential for the move to limit Reddit's reach in the short term but said it would eventually lead to more growth. "I think that's a trade that makes sense for the long term."

Since going public in early 2024, the San Francisco-based company's digital advertising business has grown rapidly. For the first time, Reddit on Thursday forecast $1 billion-plus in quarterly sales. But investors' expectations are high. Though the company said it expects fourth-quarter revenue of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, the outlook missed the average Wall Street estimate of $1.05 billion.

Reddit reported third-quarter sales of $895 million, beating the average analyst estimate compiled by Bloomberg, largely driven by the continued growth of its advertising business. Daily active users increased 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million, missing the average analyst estimate of 133.5 million.

Shares of Reddit, which recently joined the S&P 500, fell as much as 13%. They were down 44% before the market close on Thursday. Even as the ads business grows, Wall Street is hyper-focused on how Reddit will attract and retain users in the age of artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Mortgage rates fall to under 7.25 percent
articles.summary: Welcome to The Hill’s Business & Economy newsletter {beacon} Business & Economy Business & Economy Business & Economy The Big Story Mortgage rates fall to under 7.25 percent Mortgage rates declined for the second straight week, providing prospective homebuyers with a bit of relief in a pricey housing market. © Nam Y. Huh, Associated…
articles.body:
Mortgage rates fall to under 7.25 percent

Mortgage rates declined for the second straight week , providing prospective homebuyers with a bit of relief in a pricey housing market.

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.24 percent this week , down from 7.32 percent last week, according to new data from Freddie Mac.

The average 30-year mortgage rate previously dipped from 7.4 percent during the week ending on Oct. 15 to last week.

Mortgage rates have risen overall this year, as higher oil prices due to the Iran war and a bond market sell-off pushed up borrowing costs. The 10-year U.S. Treasury bond yield, which the average 30-year mortgage rate tracks closely, is down roughly 5 basis points as of Thursday afternoon.

The average 30-year mortgage rate had not declined for two straight weeks since August, when it dipped from 6.69 percent to 6.65 percent across a 14-day span. At the start of this year, the average 30-year rate was less than 6.2 percent .

The average 15-year fixed mortgage rate, meanwhile, declined for the third straight week, falling to 6.6 percent .

President Trump and administration officials have taken a slew of actions geared toward housing ahead of the midterms, as Republicans face economic headwinds with voting already underway.

Trump signed an executive order last Thursday directing his administration to create a pilot program to cancel insurance premiums for government-backed mortgages once a borrower has satisfied equity requirements.

That same day, the Treasury Department proposed barring institutional investors from buying single-family homes. The department proposed the regulations under a bipartisan housing law Congress passed over the summer — a measure the president refused to sign due to Senate Republicans’ inability to pass voter ID legislation.

Also on Thursday, the National Association of Realtors (NAR) reported that home prices rose in 78 percent of metro markets in the third quarter, down from 80 percent in the second quarter.

articles.title: 35 states, DC reach $220M settlement with General Motors over driver data privacy
articles.summary: Automaker General Motors (GM) agreed to pay $220 million to settle a lawsuit with 35 states and Washington, D.C., which alleged the company sold drivers’ data to insurance companies, several attorneys general involved with the settlement announced Thursday. A bipartisan coalition of state attorneys general, led by Democrats Dan Rayfield of Oregon and Nick Brown…
articles.body:
Automaker General Motors (GM) agreed to pay $220 million to settle a lawsuit with 35 states and Washington, D.C., which alleged the company sold drivers’ data to insurance companies, several attorneys general involved with the settlement announced Thursday.

A bipartisan coalition of state attorneys general, led by Democrats Dan Rayfield of Oregon and Nick Brown of Washington state, brought forward the challenge against the U.S.-based car manufacturer. GM did not admit wrongdoing in the settlement.

The allegations center around GM’s Smart Driver program, in which customers could enroll when they purchased a car at the dealership to track their driver safety record and encourage safe practices. The states accused the automaker of selling user information and driving data to data brokers — who sold it to insurance companies — without enrolled drivers’ knowledge.

Brown said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement that the data was often personal and included highly specific information about the drivers’ behavior.

“The data GM sold was personal, identifiable, and specific. Insurers had data showing how many times a person drove their vehicle, the start and end times of each drive, how many times they braked or accelerated quickly, and whether they went faster than the speed limit,” Brown said.

A GM spokesperson told The Hill on Thursday that the settlement strengthens existing privacy practices.

“This agreement addresses Smart Driver, a product we ended in 2024, and reinforces steps we’ve taken to strengthen our privacy practices,” the spokesperson said. “GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share.”

GM has simplified its privacy statement for consumers in recent years, the company said.

Brown also said, when users attempted to check their Smart Driver enrollment, GM’s OnStar app incorrectly told more than 370,000 drivers they were not enrolled when they actually were.

The New York Times reported in March 2024 that some drivers reportedly discovered their insurance rates had increased without any accidents — and some had trouble obtaining an insurer at all — due to driver data provided by GM.

GM has since discontinued the program, which started in 2016.

Several state attorneys general touted the ruling on social media, including Ohio’s Andy Wilson (R), Virginia’s Jay Jones (D), Colorado’s Phil Weiser (D) and New York’s Letitia James (D).

“My office is proud to defend Virginians’ privacy rights,” Jones wrote on social platform X .

After the revelations about the Smart Driver program, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) took action against GM in January 2025, banning it from disclosing certain driver data to consumer reporting agencies for five years. The FTC also mandated that GM give consumers a way to request the deletion of their data.

Texas sued GM in 2024 over the program and thus was not part of the latest settlement. That lawsuit is ongoing.

articles.title: Coinbase reports Q3 revenue decline amid crypto slump
articles.summary: Coinbase reported Q3 earnings on Thursday after the bell.
articles.body:
Coinbase Global ( COIN ) reported a plunge in Q3 revenue as the crypto industry's ongoing slump weighed on transaction sales.

Net revenue totaled $1.16 billion, down 34% from $1.76 billion a year ago. Shares sank 2% in extended trading on Thursday.

The company reported net income of $719 million for the period, or $2.15 per share, compared with a profit of $433 million a year ago. Analysts were expecting a net loss of $35 million and revenue of $1.21 billion.

Much of the profit, however, came from a $715 million gain on cryptocurrency investments. After excluding investment gains and related tax effects, Coinbase reported adjusted net income of just $78 million.

Adjusted EBITDA fell 58% to $333 million, though it rose 60% from the second quarter.

This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

The results come as Coinbase's stock has fallen 29% so far in 2026 as of its Thursday closing price, putting its yearly performance on pace to be its worst since the crypto world's 2022 crash when shares plunged 86%.

The company's transaction revenue, which is closely tied to cryptocurrency trading activity, fell 44% from a year earlier to $590 million as crypto volatility reached multiyear lows while bitcoin climbed from $60,000 to $83,000.

Coinbase has sought to expand into new businesses and product lines as it seeks to build a crypto-centric flavor of the all-in one finance app it and rivals including Robinhood (HOOD) have hotly pursued.

The company said its newer prediction markets business surpassed $200 million in annualized revenue. Daily traders on the platform increased more than 60% from the previous quarter.

"Prediction markets have been one of the fastest-growing products in Coinbase history, growing even through slower sports months driven by crypto contracts where we have a strong right to win," said CEO Brian Armstrong in a press release.

In an initial reaction Mizuho analyst Dan Dolev wrote to clients that Coinbase's results were "better than feared but crypto remains challenged."

Next week's midterm elections will also be crucial for Coinbase, which has poured tens of millions of dollars into political groups as the cryptocurrency industry seeks to strengthen its influence in Washington.

The company contributed at least $35 million during the current election cycle, making it one of the industry's largest political donors, according to a June analysis by Public Citizen.

Coinbase is a major backer of Fairshake, a crypto-focused super PAC that has supported candidates from both parties, as the industry pushes Congress to establish clearer rules for digital assets.

West Texas Intermediate gained toward $103 a barrel, after swinging more than $3 in the previous session, while Brent settled near $115. A top commander briefed President Donald Trump on military options on Thursday, the Wall Street Journal reported. Global benchmark Brent has rallied by 12% in October, hitting a six-month high, as the conflict has dragged on. The gains this month have come despite a revival of flows from the Middle East, with producers managing to ship cargoes through the Strait of Hormuz even with elevated risks to shipping.

Traders get a flood of oil supermajors' earnings this week, with results from ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. and Chevron Corp. due later Friday. On Thursday, Shell Plc Chief Executive Officer Wael Sawan said current oil prices no longer looked temporary because global inventories are so depleted.

articles.title: Shares of Google’s parent company just had their worst day ever. Here’s what it means
articles.summary: Shares of Google’s parent company tumbled more than 12% on Thursday, their worst day on record — a historic single-day decline bigger than any day during the Covid-19 pandemic or 2008 financial crisis.
articles.body: Shares of Google’s parent company tumbled more than 12% on Thursday, their worst day on record — a historic single-day decline bigger than any day during the Covid-19 pandemic or 2008 financial crisis. The drop erased roughly half a trillion dollars in Alphabet’s (GOOGL) market value, the second-largest single-day wipeout in history, after Nvidia’s nearly-$600 billion slide in early 2025. What’s going on? Investors are increasingly scrutinizing Big Tech’s AI spending spree and how the technology is affecting their own businesses — and Alphabet is their latest target. The company’s shares dropped sharply as investors fretted over slowing growth in Google’s search advertising business occurring alongside a continued ramp-up in spending on AI. The world’s largest technology companies are spending hundreds of billions of dollars to build data centers, in a race to try and be among the winners of the artificial intelligence boom. Wall Street is getting more cautious, attempting to sort out which companies are spending rationally, how those outlays are impacting other parts of their business, and who will actually benefit from AI’s transformative impact on society. Alphabet reported quarterly sales figures on Wednesday that missed analysts’ expectations. Investors were dismayed by the miss in sales figures, which reignited longstanding concerns about whether the company’s cash cow — Google’s search advertising business — will be able to withstand the pressure of consumers increasingly using Google’s own (and competitors’) AI chat bots in the place of traditional search. The fear is that this displacement might happen “faster than Google can react to it and pivot their business,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management. The company also disclosed a second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow, another metric causing concern among investors. Since going public in 2004, Google — which became Alphabet in 2015 — hadn’t posted a single quarter of negative free cash flow until this year. Strong free cash flow is one sign of a healthy company that can pay dividends, conduct share buybacks and reinvest in its business. Alphabet recorded $51.4 billion in capital expenditures in the third quarter alone, compared to $91.4 billion for the entire year in 2025. As the company ramps up its spending on AI, including data center construction, it’s leaving less cash for the kind of immediate gratification investors love, like share buybacks and dividends. In stark contrast to Alphabet’s negative free cash flow, Microsoft reported this week that it had $18.6 billion in free cash flow in the third quarter, even as it continues to spend billions on its AI buildout. Microsoft’s shares ended the day flat on Thursday while Alphabet shares dropped more than 12%. “We are now getting to see who is spending rationally on AI and who is not,” said Richard Reyle, chief investment officer at Questar Capital Partners. It might seem odd that shares of one of Big Tech’s biggest companies aren’t soaring after Anthropic filed its highly anticipated initial public offering prospectus just days earlier. Anthropic is committing to spending a lot of money to rent compute power from tech companies like Alphabet. But that future promise isn’t guaranteed, especially if the data center buildout doesn’t go to plan or if AI isn’t as profitable as expected. Alphabet is asking investors to believe in its vision for AI and the data center buildout, while also trying to monetize AI and show it can generate strong returns from the technology. Growth in Big Tech companies’ cloud computing divisions is a sign that demand for AI continues to be robust. But the market is on edge about anything that could go wrong for the AI boom. Big Tech companies like Alphabet are turning to debt and financial markets to raise more capital to help fuel their ambitions. While companies say they are trying to keep up with demand, the competition for funds from investors is rising. “Everybody is trying to get through the door at the same time, and it gives people pause,” said Ted Mortonson, an investment strategist at Baird who focuses on the tech sector. Wall Street is becoming more disconcerting about the data center buildout, and companies that are burning through free cash flow are getting punished.

articles.title: Fears of Binance hack prompt Tether, Circle to freeze over $1.5 billion in funds
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance is investigating a potential hack after a series of very large transfers on the platform caught the attention of traders.
articles.body: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said Thursday it was investigating a “potential security issue” but insisted that all customer money was safe after a series of very large transfers on the platform caught the attention of traders and the site’s founder speculated that it may have been due to a hack. “Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating. Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” a spokesperson for Binance said in a statement. “Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency,” the spokesperson said, urging users to “remain cautious of scams.” Binance is the world’s largest cryptocurrency trading platform by volume, with hundreds of thousands of users who buy, sell and store billions of dollars’ worth of digital currencies on the exchange. Unlike traditional bank deposits, money kept in accounts with companies like Binance is not insured by the government against losses, potentially leaving any refunds up to the discretion of individual exchanges. In the wake of Thursday’s reports, two major digital stablecoin issuers said they had taken steps to limit potential fallout if the Binance transfers turn out to be the result of a hacking attempt. Tether froze more than $1.567 billion worth of its digital currency “related to a potential Binance exchange hack,” CEO Paolo Ardoino said in a post on X. Jeremy Allaire, CEO of stablecoin issuer Circle, said the company had also frozen assets and was coordinating with law enforcement on the matter. “Circle is closely tracking reports of a potential exploit involving Binance. In coordination with law enforcement, we have frozen more than 800M USDC associated with the incident and will continue supporting the investigation,” he wrote, using the shorthand for the company’s United States Dollar Coin, whose value is pegged to the dollar. The sudden outflow from Binance, which was reported earlier by Bloomberg, occurred at a moment when cybersecurity defenses around the world are on high alert about the possibility of novel attacks facilitated by recent advances in artificial intelligence. Digital currency has been a primary target of hackers for years. In 2025, Coinbase disclosed that thieves had stolen customers’ personal information and attempted to extort the company for $20 million. Coinbase refused to pay and offered a bounty for information leading to arrests instead. Binance’s founder, Changpeng Zhao, said, “It does look like a hack on Binance.” “As a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered,” he wrote on X, saying user funds “are safe.” Zhao stepped down as the CEO of Binance in 2023 and pleaded guilty to breaking U.S. anti-money laundering laws. President Donald Trump later granted him a full pardon.

articles.title: Intel says it’s selling every affordable laptop chip it can make
articles.summary: Intel said in its Q3 2026 earnings call that its low-cost Wildcat Lake chips are sold out, and it’s expecting the RAM shortage to last until at least early next year.
articles.body: During Intel’s latest earnings call, CEO Lip-Bu Tan said that demand for its budget-focused Wildcat Lake chips “is outstripping supply.” According to CFO David Zinsner, the chips are now sold out. Zinsner said Intel has “seen significant growth in Wildcat Lake. It’s coming exactly at the right time because it’s cost-optimized and we’re seeing a lot of focus in that regard.” As shortages of RAM and other components have driven up PC prices over recent months, Intel’s Wildcat Lake chips have been appearing in new lower-cost Windows laptops on par with the MacBook Neo, like the new Dell XPS 13 or the HP Omnibook 5 14. Wildcat Lake laptops like these have budget-friendly starting prices, but often with just 8GB of RAM, which Windows laptops can struggle to get by on. Intel doesn’t expect the memory shortage to improve any time soon. Zinsner responded to a question about memory supply, saying, “Make no mistake, we are not optimistic about next year in terms of memory.” He added, “we’ll, you know, have to see in ‘28 whether things improve, but our expectation is that it does not improve in ‘27.” That’s more optimistic than SK Hynix’s prediction that the RAM shortage will drag on through 2030. Tan also acknowledged the PC demand slowdown, saying, “The industry continues to navigate one of the most significant supply shortages in the [sic] history, driven by the unprecedented demand for super intelligence,” referring to AI. Zinsner went on to respond to a question during the earnings call, saying, “We do think the PC is going to go through a renaissance despite this.”

articles.title: Noel picks top lawyer, friend as Trent successor
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Noel Tata has selected close friend and AZB & Partners co-founder Bahram Vakil to succeed him as chairman of Trent, the Tata Group's fashion and
articles.body: MUMBAI: Noel Tata has selected close friend and AZB & Partners co-founder Bahram Vakil to succeed him as chairman of Trent, the Tata Group's fashion and retail flagship established by his mother, Simone Tata. Vakil will take over as chairman of Trent on Nov 12, a day after Noel retires from the board-led role at the retailer on Nov 11.Vakil's appointment, however, has raised eyebrows within sections of the Tata ecosystem, according to people familiar with the matter. They said Noel did not keep Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran, who was in Singapore, informed about the board changes at Trent, particularly Vakil's elevation as chairman, before the decision was disclosed to stock exchanges on Thursday.The move comes despite Tata Sons, which owns 32% of Trent, having recently participated in the retailer's Rs 2,500-crore rights issue. While Trent has traditionally been overseen by Simone and later Noel, people said Ratan Tata, during his tenure as chairman of Tata Sons, largely refrained from intervening in the fashion retailer's affairs. The same, they said, was true of Cyrus Mistry, Ratan Tata's successor, and later Chandrasekaran.Vakil was appointed a non-executive director of Trent in April. Noel, who has been associated with Trent since 1997, will become chairman emeritus from Nov 12, a title Simone held until her death in Dec 2025. Chairman emeritus is an honorary position conferred on a retired leader and carries neither executive authority nor statutory voting rights. People said Noel and his wife, Aloo Tata, are expected to attend the wedding celebrations of Vakil's daughter at the Taj Aravali Resort & Spa in Udaipur on Friday.Vakil, people said, is also seen as a strong contender to succeed Noel as chairman of Tata Investment when he retires from the role on Nov 11. Vakil currently serves as vice-chairman of the investment company.Vakil's elevation comes amid a broader reshaping of Trent's board. The retailer has appointed Rajiv Dube, a former senior executive at Tata Motors, as a non-executive director and senior lawyer Kalpana Merchant as an independent director, effective Oct 30.
